description: Every motif row from each sample's XSTREME output (xstreme.tsv), de novo and known.
SEA statistics XSTREME reported for every motif it scored in each sample (sea_out/sea.tsv).
One row per sample summarising its XSTREME run.
Every de novo motif from every sample, with its cross-run motif family, best known-motif match and sample metadata.
Motif family x sample: occurrence of each family in each sample's peaks versus a genomic background (FIMO rescans).
Wide version of table02_motif_prevalence: % of peaks with the motif family, one column per sample.
One row per motif family: evidence that the motif derives from repetitive DNA rather than a binding site.
Sample x repeat/CenSat class: observed peak overlaps versus a shuffled-peak null model.
Wide matrix of log2(observed/expected) peak enrichment for CenSat classes, one column per sample.
Wide matrix of log2(observed/expected) peak enrichment for RepeatMasker classes, one column per sample.
Peaks in each CenSat class on each chromosome, summed over all samples.
Each sample's repeat-class overlap compared with the pooled set of regions from all samples (Fisher's exact test).
Read-level signal: fraction of IP and control reads in each repeat/CenSat class (only if reads_in_repeats is enabled).
One row per known motif with any evidence: SEA enrichment across samples and Tomtom similarity to de novo motifs.
Known-motif evidence collapsed by TF structural class (or TF name when no class table was supplied).
Up to 5 best known-motif matches (Tomtom) for each motif family representative.
SEA result for every known motif reported as enriched in every sample.
Every merged region (union of all samples' peaks) with recurrence, annotation and artifact flags.
The top-N merged regions ranked by number of samples, then number of distinct conditions.
Pairwise Jaccard similarity of samples' peak sets (square matrix).
Genome bins with peaks in the most samples (top 200).
One row per sample: metadata and every numeric feature used in the metadata models.
Linear-model effects of each covariate term on each sample feature (all covariates fitted jointly; no run/batch term).
How strongly each pair of metadata covariates is associated; high values mean their effects cannot be separated.
Per time-course series and feature: linear trend with time.
Whether the time trend of a feature differs between series (time x series interaction).
Association between detection of each motif family / known motif and each covariate.
PERMANOVA: variance in each block of sample features explained by each covariate (marginal tests).
